A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FrameBridge. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-to-video benchmark results, SAF and neural-prior ablations, and generated-video examples, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, efficiency analyses, further ablations and an 18-participant user study.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 extends SAF with output reparameterization for v-prediction models such as CogVideoX-2B, beyond v1's input and timestep alignment. The core bridge process, replicated prior and neural-prior construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds VBench-I2V evaluation inputs, including 50 sampled prompts used in the human study. WebVid-2M, UCF-101, MSR-VTT and the original class-conditional and text-conditional I2V tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the zero-shot comparator set beyond DynamiCrafter and SEINE to include SVD, ConsistI2V, SparseCtrl and I2VGen-XL. The neural-prior ablation also adds a VDT-I2V baseline conditioned on the neural prior, providing an important additional control.

E3.justification: V2 adds 100k-step fine-tuning alongside 20k steps and evaluates a CogVideoX-2B backbone. The UCF-101 SAF ablation changes from uniformly 20k iterations to 5k/10k configurations. New protocols include VBench-I2V, CD-FVD, human rankings from 18 participants on 50 prompts, and sampling-step/runtime comparisons.

E4.justification: New analyses examine motion versus consistency using noisy image conditioning and increased frame stride, FVD content bias, training convergence and sampling efficiency. V2 also adds WebVid-2M SAF ablations for both backbones and the neural-prior-conditioned diffusion control; v1 mainly ablated SAF and prior choice.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed variability, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's user-ranking averages introduce a metric and study sample size, but no uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises multiple results: SEINE's MSR-VTT FVD changes from 176 to 245, and FrameBridge's SAF result changes from 83 to 99 for the reported 20k-step configuration. V2 separately adds a 100k-step result of 95, CogVideoX results and extensive new analyses. The neural-prior diffusion control scores 132 FVD; FrameBridge-NP's original 122 remains. These are revised and additional results, not uniform performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds the mathematical construction of the aligned v-prediction output target. The bridge derivations and Propositions 1–3 with their proofs are otherwise retained. Removing the separately displayed neural-prior bridge loss from the main text is an equivalent restatement through prior substitution.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a data-to-data bridge framework for I2V, effective diffusion-to-bridge transfer through SAF, and improved generation through neural priors. Updated headline scores and broader supporting experiments do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly discusses the tradeoff between motion and consistency and the content bias of FVD. It also interprets the added curves as evidence of faster convergence and effective reduced-step sampling. The original explanation based on informative priors and frame-to-frames generation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds training/sampling pseudocode, discrete-timestep SNR interpolation details and CogVideoX implementation sources, and updates the project-page address. Most existing hyperparameters remain documented. However, v1's explicit general specification of first-order, 250-step sampling is no longer retained as such.

R1.justification: V2 expands discussion of coupled flow matching, noise calibration, newer bridge models and additional video-generation methods. It adds benchmark-related citations while retaining the central positioning against noise-to-data diffusion. Numerous venue/year updates refer to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial motivation/SAF passages are rewritten. Background and motivation are consolidated, the main experimental setup discussion is compressed, and the appendices are reorganized around new pseudocode and analysis sections, moving the original related-work appendix from B to E.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main layout, redesigns comparison tables with training-budget columns and ranking markers, and adds analytical plots, tables and algorithm boxes. Qualitative displays are reorganized: the rabbit example moves from Figure 5 to Figure 9, while v1 Figures 6–9 are retained as v2 Figures 12–15.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's limited empirical validation through broader baselines, explicit training-budget comparisons and the missing neural-prior-conditioned diffusion control. VBench-I2V, CD-FVD and human judgments better examine whether apparent gains reflect consistency at the expense of motion. Cross-backbone and efficiency analyses further support applicability. Uncertainty remains unreported and some sampling-plot labeling is inconsistent, but the added controls and complementary evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
